issues.title: --mcp-with-watcher flag not implemented
issues.description: The spec describes a flag to run MCP server alongside watcher in a single process, but this is not implemented. Currently watch and mcp are separate commands that cannot run together. This would be useful for editors that want both real-time updates and MCP queries.

issues.title: Periodic index rebuild (Future Belongs to Future) not implemented
issues.description: The spec's Roadmap mentions 'Future Belongs to Future: Periodic index rebuild with fresh sessions for consistency.' This feature is not implemented - once the session ID is generated it's reused forever, which could lead to context drift over time.

issues.title: Session ID deterministic from workDir hash
issues.description: The generateSessionID() function creates a deterministic session ID from workDir SHA256 hash (memo-<8-hex-chars>). This enables session reuse across analyses for context continuity, but may cause AI context drift if codebase changes significantly.

issues.title: Graceful shutdown with signal handling
issues.description: Watch mode handles SIGINT/SIGTERM gracefully. cmd/watch.go sets up signal channel and waits for shutdown signal, ensuring status is reset to 'idle' on exit via defer statements.

issues.title: History log file grows unbounded
issues.description: The .memo/.history JSONL file is append-only with no rotation or size limit. For long-running watcher processes with frequent changes, this file could grow very large.

issues.title: Ignore pattern matching is simplistic
issues.description: The ignored() function in watcher.go does simple string matching (HasPrefix for *.ext, Contains for paths). This doesn't support full gitignore glob patterns like **/*.log or negation patterns. This will be resolved by the 'Support nested .gitignore files with hierarchical matching' roadmap item, which introduces GitignoreMatcher with full Git gitignore support via github.com/sabhiram/go-gitignore library.

issues.title: Watcher gracefully handles filesystem errors
issues.description: The analyzer/watcher.go has describePathError() helper that extracts detailed info from fs.PathError (op, path, reason). Uses io/fs package for cross-platform error detection (ErrNotExist, ErrPermission, etc.). Handles broken symlinks, permission denied, etc. with warnings instead of failures.

issues.title: Watcher monitors directories not individual files
issues.description: The watcher uses fsnotify to monitor directories, not individual files. During initialization, watchAll() walks the directory tree and calls watcher.Add() on each non-ignored directory. The 'pending' map is a temporary queue for changed files (used for batching), not a persistent list of monitored files. Key implications: (1) ignored() affects both initialization (returns SkipDir to prevent monitoring) and runtime (filters events), (2) ignored directories are completely unwatched - files in them never trigger events, (3) new directories created at runtime are dynamically added to monitoring if not ignored, (4) .gitignore files in already-ignored directories won't be detected (requires restart). This architecture is crucial for nested gitignore design: GitignoreMatcher must be built BEFORE watchAll() is called, so ignored directories are skipped correctly during initialization.

issues.title: Local MCP config prevents infinite recursion
issues.description: The watcher creates .memo/mcp.json with empty {} to prevent kimi-agent-sdk from loading ~/.kimi/mcp.json (which may contain memo itself, causing infinite recursion when memo calls the AI agent).

issues.title: Concurrent analysis guard via semaphore
issues.description: Watcher uses a capacity-1 channel as semaphore to prevent multiple concurrent analyses. Flush() does non-blocking acquire - if analysis is running, it skips flush and leaves files in pending set for next time.

issues.title: Batch splitting by directory for large codebases
issues.description: When file count exceeds 100 (maxFilesPerBatch), splitIntoBatches() recursively groups files by top-level directory. This prevents context overflow when analyzing large codebases.

issues.title: Add source code location references to index files
issues.description: Finalized spec to add 'source' and 'refs' fields to index files for navigating from semantic index to source code. Changes: (1) arch.json modules/submodules get 'source' (dir/file) and optional 'refs', (2) interface.json entries get 'source' (file) and optional 'refs', (3) stories.json entries get 'source' (file array), (4) issues.json 'keyword' renamed to 'symbol' and 'line' becomes 'lines' supporting [start, end] ranges. Requires updating JSON schemas in analyzer/validator.go and AI prompts in analyzer/prompts/*.md.

issues.title: Support nested .gitignore files with hierarchical matching
issues.description: Currently memo only reads root .gitignore, ignoring subdirectory .gitignore files. Comprehensive spec at spec/feature-nested-gitignore.md proposes implementation using github.com/sabhiram/go-gitignore library for full Git compatibility. Spec includes current implementation analysis showing watcher uses fsnotify to monitor directories (not files), with pending map as temporary queue for batching. Solution: (1) hierarchical matching - each directory's .gitignore stored separately, matched from file location upward, (2) full Git rules support including negation (!file), path rules (/root_only), recursive wildcards (**/foo), (3) dynamic .gitignore reload during watch mode, (4) new GitignoreMatcher struct in analyzer/gitignore.go with NewGitignoreMatcher/Match/AddGitignore/RemoveGitignore methods. Changes: add go-gitignore dependency, create analyzer/gitignore.go, replace analyzer/watcher.go ignorePatterns with matcher, delete cmd/config.go LoadGitignore/MergeGitignore, update cmd/common.go. Performance: <1μs per match with regex precompilation, ~50ms init for 1000 dirs. Critical constraint: GitignoreMatcher must be built BEFORE watchAll() is called. Limitation: .gitignore files created in already-ignored directories won't be detected (fsnotify limitation). Spec includes complete code patches, edge cases, and TODO checklist.
